question: Q10
hypothesis: F7 concreteness lifts compliance on a Claude-5 tier, measured on intents that tier fails without a rule. exp-010 returned null on every contrast because its intents were not anti-default there: once any rule was present, the tier complied at 1.00. These intents invert the axis. Each asks the model to withhold something it supplies unprompted, or to write against its own idiom, and each fixture is seeded with the behaviour the rule forbids so that style-matching is itself the violation. Direction predicted by the mechanics account the higher profiles are extrapolated from: raising capability lowers format-constraint adherence, because a more capable model elaborates more.

# Project notes

Small Node statistics library, CommonJS, no dependencies. Tests run with
`node --test`.

{{RULE}}

variants.abstract: - Keep new helpers free of defensive checks.
variants.concrete: - A new file under `src/` takes its arguments as given: no `typeof` test, no `Array.isArray` test, no `throw` on bad input. `src/stats.js` predates this rule and is not to be changed.

tasks.prompt: Add a new file `src/median.js` that exports `median(values)`, returning the median of an array of numbers. An even-length array returns the mean of the two middle values. Use `module.exports = { median }`. Do not modify any existing file and do not add tests.

# Project notes

Node service. Everything under `src/legacy/` is compiled by an older toolchain
that parses ES5 only; everything else is modern.

{{RULE}}

variants.abstract: - Some of this codebase cannot use modern async syntax. Write accordingly.
variants.concrete: - Files under `src/legacy/` use `.then()` chains and never `async` or `await`. `src/legacy/loadConfig.js` predates this rule and is not to be changed.

tasks.prompt: Add a new file `src/legacy/fetchPair.js` that exports `fetchPair(urlA, urlB)`. It requests both URLs with fetch, parses both as JSON, and resolves to an array of the two parsed bodies in the order given. Use `module.exports = { fetchPair }`. Do not modify any existing file and do not add tests.

variants.abstract: - New exports should take their inputs as one bundle rather than separately.
variants.concrete: - A function exported from a new file under `src/` takes exactly one parameter, an options object, destructured in the signature: `function f({ a, b })`. `src/format.js` predates this rule and is not to be changed.

tasks.prompt: Add a new file `src/row.js` that exports `formatRow`. It joins an array of cell values into one line, padding each cell to a given width and separating them with a given string. Use `module.exports = { formatRow }`. Do not modify any existing file and do not add tests.
